sections.normalized_html:
First, we rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form to find the slope of line [MATH: f{:}]

[MATH: (4)/(7)x − (2)/(3)y + 6|= 0; − (2)/(3)y|= − (4)/(7)x − 6; y|= (6)/(7)x + 9]

So, the slope of line [MATH: f] is [MATH: \dfrac{6}{7}.]

A line perpendicular to this line has a slope that is the negative reciprocal. That means we flip the fraction and change the sign.

The reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{6}{7}] is [MATH: \dfrac{7}{6},] and taking the opposite sign gives

[MATH: m_g = -\dfrac{7}{6}.]

Therefore, the slope of line [MATH: g] is [MATH: -\dfrac{7}{6}.]
